schema_ddl:
CREATE TABLE ACTIVITY (
    PLAYER_ID INT,
    EVENT_DATE DATE,
    DEVICE_ID INT,
    GAMES_PLAYED INT,
    PRIMARY KEY (PLAYER_ID, EVENT_DATE),
    CHECK (GAMES_PLAYED >= 0)
);
q1: SELECT A1.FIRST_LOGIN AS INSTALL_DT, COUNT(DISTINCT A1.PLAYER_ID) AS INSTALLS, ROUND((SUM(CASE WHEN (A1.FIRST_LOGIN + 1) = A2.EVENT_DATE THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/ COUNT(DISTINCT A1.PLAYER_ID)), 2) AS DAY1_RETENTION FROM (SELECT PLAYER_ID, MIN(EVENT_DATE) AS FIRST_LOGIN FROM ACTIVITY GROUP BY PLAYER_ID) AS A1 JOIN ACTIVITY AS A2 ON A1.PLAYER_ID = A2.PLAYER_ID GROUP BY A1.FIRST_LOGIN
q2: SELECT FISRT_DATE AS INSTALL_DT, COUNT(DISTINCT A.PLAYER_ID) AS INSTALLS, ROUND(COUNT(EVENT_DATE)/COUNT(DISTINCT A.PLAYER_ID),2) AS DAY1_RETENTION FROM ( SELECT PLAYER_ID, MIN(EVENT_DATE) AS FISRT_DATE FROM ACTIVITY GROUP BY PLAYER_ID ) A LEFT JOIN ACTIVITY B ON A.FISRT_DATE = B.EVENT_DATE - 1 AND A.PLAYER_ID = B.PLAYER_ID GROUP BY INSTALL_DT

explanation: Both queries compute the same metrics: INSTALL_DT (first login date), INSTALLS (distinct players installed on that date), and DAY1_RETENTION (ratio of players who had an event the next day). The logic in both queries aligns: Q1 uses an INNER JOIN and SUM(CASE WHEN) to count players with events on the next day, while Q2 uses a LEFT JOIN and COUNT(EVENT_DATE) for the same purpose. Since each player has at most one event per day (due to the primary key constraint), both approaches yield identical results.
